🇾🇪🔥 The Yemeni Houthis Declared War On Saudi Arabia

Yemen’s Tehran-aligned Houthis have claimed responsibility for an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, two days after the kingdom signed ⁠a defence pact with Turkey ⁠and Pakistan in response to growing regional instability caused by the US-Israel war on Iran.

The attack early on Sunday came after Iran said tough new demands would have to be met before it would reopen the strait of Hormuz, and after the United Arab Emirates said one of its ships had been targeted by an Iranian missile, as a deal to open the waterway remained out of reach.
He added that the US must also end the naval blockade of Iranian ports and withdraw its military from the area, “completely compensate” Iran for war damage, lift sanctions and “unconditionally” release frozen assets.

There was no immediate comment from the US. According to the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by the US and Iran in June, a timetable to end sanctions and a plan for compensation would be part of a final peace deal, and negotiations would address frozen assets.
The Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said on Saturday that Iran and Oman were close to reaching an agreement on navigation through the strait, “specifically the determination of a transit route”.

But the waterway’s reopening was contingent on other conditions, Araghchi said, in remarks shared on social media. He blamed the situation on what he called the US violation of the June MoU.
Oman, which is mediating and has made relatively few comments on the Hormuz talks, said on Saturday that the discussions were continuing “in a positive and constructive atmosphere”. It condemned attacks on ships in the strait.

When it comes to decision-making in Tehran, the final say rests with the supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since an airstrike killed his father and predecessor on the first day of the war.

Pezeshkian has given differing accounts in recent ⁠weeks about his access to the supreme leader, saying in July that interactions with Khamenei were “increasing day by ‌day”, only to note weeks later that communicating with him was “very difficult”.

With Iran and the US still arguing over the parameters for peace, the Houthis last month declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea, citing what they said was a Saudi siege on them, an allegation Riyadh denies.

The Saudi energy ministry said a fire had broken out at Aramco’s Jazan refinery early on Sunday but was later extinguished with no injuries and authorities were dealing with the ⁠incident, without giving a cause.

The Houthis used a drone to target the refinery in south-west Saudi Arabia, Yahya Saree, a military spokesperson for the rebel group, said in a post on X. They had struck Aramco sites before in Jazan, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude oil a day. They had also hit Yanbu, an oil export hub ‌on the Red Sea.

In a separate statement, Saree said the Houthis had carried out missile and drone strikes on the Yemeni Red Sea port city of Mocha, which is controlled by the country’s internationally recognised, Saudi-backed governing body in Aden.

Tehran and its allied Shia armed groups have been striking Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states and blockading their ‌energy shipments since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran on 28 February.
The escalation of the conflict, which has disrupted global energy supplies and rattled the world’s economy, prompted Saudi Arabia on Friday to form an alliance with US allies Turkey and Pakistan.

📣 Brazil stablecoins face IMF scrutiny as crypto flows outpace capital 

🌐 IMF has called for closer oversight of Brazil’s stablecoin market as cross-border crypto flows outpace traditional capital movements. The report says cross-border crypto transactions have increased faster than conventional capital flows and now require closer regulatory attention because of their growing links with the country’s financial system. The assessment says stablecoin purchases respond much more strongly to global financial shocks than traditional portfolio investment or foreign direct investment. 

🔔 Based on the IMF’s analysis, purchases of dollar-backed stablecoins are two to three times more sensitive to external market events, raising concerns over how quickly international volatility could spread through crypto markets. Brazil has emerged as one of the world’s more active crypto markets, with stablecoins accounting for a significant share of digital asset activity. The IMF said the country’s crypto ecosystem has become increasingly connected with the traditional financial sector, making regulatory oversight more important as adoption continues to rise.

⚠️ The report acknowledges that Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) has already introduced measures to regulate crypto asset service providers. Even so, the IMF said several areas still need stronger rules, including customer asset protection, stablecoin issuance requirements, and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CFT) standards.

🔻 Pezeshkian congratulates appointments of new Armed Forces chief, deputy

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has congratulated Major General Ali Abdollahi and Brigadier General Kioumars Heidari on their appointments as commander and deputy commander of the General Staff of the Armed Forces, stressing the need to strengthen coordination, preparedness and the country’s defense capabilities.

In separate messages, Pezeshkian said the extensive command experience of both military commanders will provide an important foundation for carrying out their new responsibilities.
​
Regarding General Abdollahi’s appointment, the President  said, “Your valuable experience in various fields of command and your effective presence in the field of defending the country will be a valuable asset for carrying out this important responsibility.”
​
He added that protecting Iran’s security, independence and territorial integrity required vigilance, coordination and comprehensive preparedness, describing the new General Staff of the Armed Forces as holding a prominent and strategic position.
​
Pezeshkian said Iran’s strength depended not only on its defense capabilities but also on the cohesion and synergy of its armed forces and the use of the country’s knowledge, experience and modern defense capacities.
​
“I am confident that with a strategic and forward-looking approach, you will make valuable contributions to strengthening coordination among the armed forces and enhancing the country’s deterrence capabilities,” he said.
​
The president also said that his government regarded the armed forces as pillars of the country’s power, security and independence and emphasized the need for synergy and coordination among all parts of the system to safeguard national security, national interests and territorial integrity.
​
Pezeshkian also paid tribute to the late Major General Martyr Seyyed Abdolrahim Mousavi, expressing hope that Abdollahi would succeed in his assigned missions under divine guidance and the directives of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces.
​
In his separate message to General Heidari, President Pezeshkian congratulated him on his appointment as deputy chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces and highlighted his command experience and knowledge of the requirements of the armed forces.
​
“Undoubtedly, your valuable experience in the field of command and your precise understanding of the requirements of the armed forces are an important asset for carrying out this mission,” Pezeshkian said.
​
He said that amid increasingly complex and multilayered threats and opportunities facing the country, strengthening preparedness, coordination among forces and the use of valuable defense and operational experience were strategic necessities.
​
Pezeshkian expressed hope that Heidari would succeed in his assigned missions, while paying tribute to all martyrs, particularly the “proud martyred commanders and generals” of Iran.
